subject: maths
title: Chapter 2 · Test 3
summary: Chapter 2 test 3: parallel lines, triangle angle sums, quadrilateral properties, and interior and exterior angles of polygons.
body: This test covers Chapter 2: angles and parallel lines, angle sums of triangles, properties of quadrilaterals, interior angles of polygons and exterior angles. It has 15 questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes. Work with no notes and no calculator unless the question says. Diagrams are drawn to scale, but always use the angle rules and the facts you are given — never measure. Write your working, give a reason for each step, and check that your answer is the angle the question asks for (not just the value of x).

questions.prompt: AB ∥ CD. In the diagram, the angle above CD on the left of the transversal is 58°. Find x, the matching angle above AB.
questions.explanation: x and 58° are in the same position at each crossing (above the line, left of the transversal), so they are corresponding angles and are equal: x = 58. 122 treats them as adding to 180°.
steps: Both angles are above their parallel line and on the left of the transversal — the same position at each crossing.
These are corresponding angles (F shape), which are equal when the lines are parallel.

mistakes.A: Step 2: corresponding angles are equal — they do not add to 180°.
mistakes.B: Step 2: there is no right angle here, so do not subtract from 90°.
mistakes.D: Step 2: corresponding angles are equal — do not double the angle.

questions.diagram_alt: Parallel lines AB and CD cut by a transversal at P and Q. Above AB, left of the transversal, the angle is x; above CD, left of the transversal, the angle is 58°

questions.prompt: In the diagram, AB = AC and ∠BAC = 80°. Find x.
questions.explanation: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, so x = (180 − 80) ÷ 2 = 50. 100 forgets to share between the two base angles.
steps: AB = AC, so the base angles at B and C are equal.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 100° is the two base angles together. Halve it.
mistakes.B: Step 2: subtract 80 from 180 first, then halve. 80 ÷ 2 halves the wrong angle.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the equal angles are the base angles at B and C, not the angle at A.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with AB and AC marked equal. Angle BAC is 80° and angle ABC is marked x

questions.prompt: The hexagon in the diagram has angles 130°, 115°, 120°, 140°, 100° and x°. Find x.
questions.explanation: A hexagon's angles add to (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°. The known angles add to 605°, so x = 720 − 605 = 115. 295 uses 900°, the sum for a heptagon.

mistakes.B: Step 1: a hexagon's angle sum is (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°, not 900°.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 65° would be the exterior angle. x is the interior angle: 720 − 605.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 605 is the total of the five known angles. Subtract it from 720.

questions.diagram_alt: Hexagon ABCDEF with interior angles A = 130°, B = 115°, C = 120°, D = 140°, E = 100° and F = x°

questions.prompt: The diagram shows a regular nonagon (9 sides) with one side extended. Find the exterior angle x.
questions.explanation: The 9 equal exterior angles add to 360°, so x = 360 ÷ 9 = 40°. 140° is the interior angle.
steps: The exterior angles of a convex polygon add to 360°.
A regular nonagon has 9 equal exterior angles.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 140° is the interior angle. x is the exterior angle, the turn at the corner.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the exterior angles add to 360°, not 180°.
mistakes.D: Step 2: a nonagon has 9 sides, so divide 360 by 9, not 8.

questions.diagram_alt: Regular nonagon with all sides equal. One side is extended (dashed) and the exterior angle between the extension and the next side is marked x

questions.prompt: AB ∥ CD. In the diagram, ∠BPQ = (5x − 20)° and ∠PQD = (3x + 40)°. Find ∠PQD.
questions.explanation: ∠BPQ and ∠PQD are co-interior, so 8x + 20 = 180, giving x = 20 and ∠PQD = 3 × 20 + 40 = 100°. Setting them equal (x = 30) gives 130°, which treats them as alternate angles.
steps: ∠BPQ and ∠PQD are between the parallel lines on the same side of PQ — co-interior, so they add to 180°: 5x − 20 + 3x + 40 = 180.
Collect like terms: 8x + 20 = 180, so 8x = 160 and x = 20.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 80° is ∠BPQ (5x − 20). The question asks for ∠PQD = 3x + 40.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 20 is the value of x. Substitute it into 3x + 40.
mistakes.C: Step 1: these angles are co-interior (same side, between the lines), so they add to 180° — do not set them equal.

questions.diagram_alt: Parallel lines AB and CD cut by a transversal at P and Q. Angle BPQ (right of the transversal, below AB) is (5x − 20)° and angle PQD (right of the transversal, above CD) is (3x + 40)°

questions.prompt: In the diagram, side BC of triangle ABC is extended to D. ∠A = 50°, ∠B = (x + 12)° and the exterior angle ∠ACD = 2x°. Find the size of ∠ACD.
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = sum of the interior opposite angles: 2x = 50 + x + 12, so x = 62 and ∠ACD = 124°. 62 is only x.
steps: Exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles: 2x = 50 + (x + 12).
Subtract x from both sides: x = 62.

mistakes.B: Step 2: 62 is the value of x. The exterior angle is 2x, so double it.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 56° is the interior angle ∠ACB. ∠ACD is the exterior angle next to it.
mistakes.D: Step 1: include the + 12 in ∠B: 2x = 50 + x + 12, not 2x = 50 + x.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with side BC extended past C to D. Angle A is 50°, angle B is (x + 12)° and the exterior angle ACD is 2x°

questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram with diagonal BD. ∠ABD = 48° and ∠ADB = 37°. Find ∠BCD.
questions.explanation: In triangle ABD, ∠BAD = 180 − 48 − 37 = 95°. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so ∠BCD = ∠BAD = 95°. 85° stops at 48 + 37.
steps: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so ∠BCD = ∠BAD = 95°.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 85° is 48 + 37. Subtract it from 180° to get ∠BAD first.
mistakes.C: Step 3: ∠BCD is a corner angle of the parallelogram, not part of the diagonal angle at B.
mistakes.D: Step 2: use the angle sum of triangle ABD (both 48° and 37°), not just 180 − 48.

questions.diagram_alt: Parallelogram ABCD with diagonal BD. Angle ABD is 48°, angle ADB is 37°, and angle BCD is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: The diagram shows a regular polygon with 20 sides. Find the size of each interior angle.
questions.explanation: The angle sum is (20 − 2) × 180 = 3240°, shared equally between 20 angles: 3240 ÷ 20 = 162°. 18° is the exterior angle.
steps: All 20 angles are equal, so divide by 20.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 18° is the exterior angle (360 ÷ 20). The interior angle is 180° minus it.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 3240° is the sum of all 20 angles. Divide by 20.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the angle sum uses n − 2 = 18 triangles, not n − 1 = 19.

questions.diagram_alt: A regular polygon with 20 equal sides; one interior angle is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: The diagram shows the four exterior angles of a quadrilateral: 95°, 85°, 2x° and x°. Find x.
questions.explanation: Exterior angles add to 360°: 95 + 85 + 3x = 360, so 3x = 180 and x = 60. 120 is the value of 2x, not x.
steps: The exterior angles of a convex polygon add to 360°: 95 + 85 + 2x + x = 360.

mistakes.B: Step 3: 120 is 2x, the other exterior angle. The question asks for x.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 3x = 180, so divide by 3, not by 2.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 3x = 180 is not finished — divide both sides by 3.

questions.diagram_alt: Quadrilateral ABCD with each side extended. The exterior angles are 95° at A, 85° at B, 2x° at C and x° at D

questions.prompt: AB ∥ CD and the line bends at E, as shown. ∠ABE = 3y°, ∠CDE = (y + 34)° and ∠BED = (6y − 10)°. Find ∠BED.
questions.explanation: The tip angle equals the sum of the arm angles: 6y − 10 = 3y + y + 34, so 2y = 44, y = 22 and ∠BED = 6 × 22 − 10 = 122°. 22 is only y.
steps: Arrowhead rule (draw a line through E parallel to AB): ∠BED = ∠ABE + ∠CDE, so 6y − 10 = 3y + y + 34.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 22 is the value of y. Substitute it into 6y − 10.
mistakes.C: Step 3: ∠BED is the whole tip angle, 6y − 10, not half of it.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 66° is ∠ABE (3y), one arm angle. The tip angle is the sum of both arm angles.

questions.diagram_alt: Parallel lines AB and CD with a line bending at E between them, like an arrowhead pointing right. Angle ABE is 3y°, angle CDE is (y + 34)° and angle BED is (6y − 10)°

questions.prompt: In the diagram, D is on BC and AB = AD. ∠BAD = 40° and ∠ACB = 25°. Find ∠DAC.
questions.explanation: AB = AD gives base angles of (180 − 40) ÷ 2 = 70°, so ∠ADB = 70° and ∠ADC = 110°. In triangle ADC, ∠DAC = 180 − 110 − 25 = 45°. 70° is ∠ADB, not ∠DAC.
steps: AB = AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles: ∠ADB = ∠ABD = (180 − 40) ÷ 2 = 70°.
Angles on the straight line BC: ∠ADC = 180 − 70 = 110°.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 70° is ∠ADB, a base angle of triangle ABD. Keep going to triangle ADC.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 110° is ∠ADC. ∠DAC is the third angle of triangle ADC.
mistakes.C: Step 2: ∠ADC is on a straight line with ∠ADB, so it is 180 − 70 = 110°, not 70°.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with point D on BC and segment AD. AB and AD are marked equal. Angle BAD is 40°, angle ACB is 25°, and angle DAC is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: A heptagon (7 sides) has five angles of 130° and two equal angles of x°, as shown. Find x.
questions.explanation: A heptagon's angles add to (7 − 2) × 180 = 900°. The five 130° angles make 650°, so 2x = 250 and x = 125. 250 forgets to share between the two angles.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 250 is the two x angles together. Divide by 2.
mistakes.B: Step 1: a heptagon's angle sum is (7 − 2) × 180 = 900°, not 1080°.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 55 would be the exterior angle. x is the interior angle.

questions.diagram_alt: Heptagon ABCDEFG with interior angles of 130° at A, B, D, E and G, and x° at C and F

questions.prompt: ABCD is a rhombus with diagonal BD. ∠ABD = 2x° and ∠ADB = (x + 22)°. Find ∠DBC.
questions.explanation: AB = AD, so ∠ABD = ∠ADB: 2x = x + 22, x = 22 and ∠ABD = 44°. The diagonal of a rhombus halves the corner angle, so ∠DBC = ∠ABD = 44°. 88° is the whole of ∠ABC.
steps: In a rhombus AB = AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles and ∠ABD = ∠ADB: 2x = x + 22.
Subtract x from both sides: x = 22, so ∠ABD = 2 × 22 = 44°.
A rhombus diagonal cuts the corner angle in half, so ∠DBC = ∠ABD = 44°.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 92° is ∠BAD. ∠DBC is the part of the angle at B on the other side of the diagonal.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 22 is the value of x. Substitute it back: ∠ABD = 2x.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 88° is the whole angle ∠ABC. The diagonal cuts it in half; ∠DBC is one half.

questions.diagram_alt: Rhombus ABCD with all sides marked equal and diagonal BD. Angle ABD is 2x°, angle ADB is (x + 22)°, and angle DBC is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: ABCDE is a regular pentagon. Sides AB and DC are extended past B and C until they meet at P. Find ∠BPC.
questions.explanation: The angles of triangle BPC at B and C are exterior angles of the pentagon, each 360 ÷ 5 = 72°. So ∠BPC = 180 − 72 − 72 = 36°. 72° is an exterior angle, not ∠BPC.
steps: ∠PBC and ∠PCB are exterior angles of the pentagon (AB and DC are extended).
Each exterior angle of a regular pentagon is 360 ÷ 5 = 72°.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 72° is the exterior angle at B (and at C). ∠BPC is the third angle of triangle BPC.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 108° is the interior angle of the pentagon. The angles of triangle BPC at B and C are exterior angles.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 144° is the two exterior angles together. Subtract it from 180°.

questions.diagram_alt: Regular pentagon ABCDE with all sides marked equal. Sides AB and DC are extended (dashed) past B and C to meet at P. Angle BPC is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: ABCD is a square. E is on side BC with ∠BAE = 25°. Line AE meets the diagonal BD at F. Find ∠AFB.
questions.explanation: The diagonal of a square cuts the 90° corner in half, so ∠ABF = 45°. In triangle ABF, ∠AFB = 180 − 25 − 45 = 110°. 70° is ∠AFD, the angle next to it.
steps: The diagonal BD of a square cuts the right angle at B in half, so ∠ABD = 45°.
In triangle ABF, the angles are ∠BAF = 25° and ∠ABF = 45°.

mistakes.B: Step 3: 70° is ∠AFD, on the other side of BD. ∠AFB is inside triangle ABF.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 65° is 90 − 25 = ∠EAD. Use the 45° angle that the diagonal makes at B.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 135° is 180 − 45 and ignores the 25° angle. Use all three angles of triangle ABF.
